ideas.risks: The proposed lower-bound survival law may fail at jump or accumulation points; exact attainment is impossible under strict crossing, so the theorem must be phrased as an infimum or eta-implementation.
ideas.summary: Ask an explorer to fully prove or break the compact-menu local theorem. For compact C, m=max C, successor s_C(x)=min(C cap [x,m]), and delta(C) defined by integral_delta^m dx/s_C(x)=1, verify existence, uniqueness, measurability, the primal distribution with density dx/s_C(x), and a dual threshold law supported on C giving the matching lower bound. Stress-test singleton menus, finite menus, Cantor-like menus, and menus accumulating at 0.
ideas.title: Audit Compact-Menu Local Lemma
ideas.why_promising: This is the main new solver contribution and would naturally become the infinite-menu analogue of the accepted finite-menu formula.

ideas.risks: The bound may remain only sufficient because sup_a sum_t rewards can be much smaller than sum_t M_{t,T}; explorers should avoid claiming necessity too quickly.
ideas.summary: Develop the suffix-menu upper theorem rigorously: for a deterministic exogenous path, C_t=closure{M_{t,T}:T>t}, choose eta-implemented local compact-menu distributions at each t, and prove R_T <= sum_{t<T} delta(C_t)+o(T) uniformly over horizons. Evaluate sum delta(C_t) on sparse vanishing spikes, power-of-two spikes, superexponential uniform spikes, equal-revenue blocks, and monotone threshold runs.
ideas.title: Path-Dependent Suffix-Menu Sufficiency
ideas.why_promising: It turns the compact local lemma into a genuine known-path anytime sufficient condition and tests whether it explains both easy and hard examples already in the notes.

ideas.risks: A matching lower bound may be false because local dual thresholds for different t need not align with a single evaluation horizon or a single fixed comparator.
ideas.summary: Investigate whether large sum_t delta(C_t) forces large horizon-oblivious regret, and if not, identify the exact obstruction. Try to align local dual laws by choosing horizons that realize many hard suffix thresholds simultaneously; conversely search for paths where sum delta(C_t) is linear but one fixed comparator coupling makes regret sublinear.
ideas.title: Is Sum Delta Necessary?
ideas.why_promising: This targets the solver's main gap and could either produce a path-dependent characterization or a useful counterexample showing why the local upper framework is loose.

ideas.risks: The resulting LP may be infinite-dimensional and hard to solve; finite prefixes may give misleading structure unless strict-crossing left limits are handled carefully.
ideas.summary: Formulate the exact known-path horizon-oblivious offline design problem for a finite deterministic path as an LP: choose quote distributions mu_t to minimize sup_T [V_T^* - sum_{t<T} g_{mu_t}(M_{t,T})]. Derive the dual and compare its value to sum_t delta(C_t), the 1/e worst-case theorem, and the multi-threshold block lower bounds.
ideas.title: Global LP Instead Of Local Menus
ideas.why_promising: It avoids the loose comparator upper bound V_T^* <= sum_t M_{t,T} and may reveal the right path-dependent quantity.

ideas.risks: Known robust-pricing results may cover only interval supports, ratios, moment information, or different benchmark conventions, so the map to the delayed-fill local game must be exact.
ideas.summary: Have an explorer map the compact-menu game to support-only minimax-regret pricing without priors. Check whether Bergemann-Schlag, Kocyigit-Rujeerapaiboon-Kuhn, or Wang-Liu-Zhang already imply the interval or arbitrary-support version, and identify exactly which parts remain internal to this project.
ideas.title: Robust-Pricing Literature Map
ideas.why_promising: The solver's successor-density construction is very close to randomized robust pricing; a precise citation could prevent duplicating known minimax geometry.

ideas.risks: Conditioning on support-valued random future menus can become tautological or nonimplementable if the learner lacks computable conditional support information.
ideas.summary: Extend the deterministic suffix-menu condition to exogenous stochastic processes. At time t and history F_t, define a conditional support menu for future suffix maxima over all horizons, assign a random local delta_t(F_t), and try to prove expected regret bounds by E sum_t delta_t plus eta terms. Test rare-history essential-sup examples to see whether probability weighting fixes beta/gamma pathologies.
ideas.title: Conditional Support-Menus For Stochastic Paths
ideas.why_promising: This could convert the known-path theorem into a nontrivial process-aware but horizon-oblivious stochastic sufficiency condition, while respecting the rare-history obstructions.

ideas.risks: Existing derandomization only handles one fixed equal-revenue law and monotone threshold sequences; nonidentical menu-dependent laws may require much stronger discrepancy tools.
ideas.summary: Try to derandomize the path-dependent suffix-menu policies. Given nonidentical local distributions mu_t from compact menus, seek a deterministic quote sequence that preserves all horizon payoffs up to o(T), perhaps via finite-grid union bounds, online rounding, or low-discrepancy constructions.
ideas.title: Derandomize Menu-Adaptive Policies
ideas.why_promising: Iteration 10 handled the universal 1/e law; a menu-adaptive derandomization would strengthen the new path-dependent sufficient condition and clarify deterministic policy power.

ideas.risks: The obstruction may be obvious but still useful only as a scope note, not a deep theorem.
ideas.summary: Probe the exact failure under endogenous or reactive prices. Construct small examples where future prices depend on the realized quote so M_{t,T} is not independent of A_t, breaking g_mu(M_{t,T}); determine whether any weakened suffix-menu argument survives under oblivious adversaries, adaptive adversaries, or prices depending only on past but not current quotes.
ideas.title: Endogeneity Boundary For Suffix Max
ideas.why_promising: The accepted 1/e and compact-menu arguments all rely on exogeneity; a crisp boundary result would prevent overextension and sharpen theorem statements.
